papers.abstract_en: Tarlatamab, a delta-like protein 3 (DLL3) × CD3-directed T cell engager (TCE), provides clinical efficacy against small cell lung cancers (SCLCs), although its efficacy remains limited, indicating the importance of clarifying the resistance mechanisms. We show that serotonin (5-HT) produced by DLL3high neuroendocrine cancers (NECs) induces immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), resulting in impaired CD8+ T cell function and TCE resistance. Using SCLC and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma cohorts, we find that DLL3high SCLCs induce immunosuppressive TAMs in the tumor microenvironment and become resistant to tarlatamab. DLL3high NECs increase 5-HT production via TPH1 upregulation. NEC-derived 5-HT augments the immunosuppressive activity of 5-HT receptor 7 (HTR7)-expressing TAMs. Genetic ablation of HTR7 in TAMs or TPH1 in NECs restores CD8+ T cell function and improves the efficacy of TCEs and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade. We propose that NEC-derived 5-HT-HTR7 axis drives immunosuppressive TAM activation and TCE resistance, making it a key target to increase TCE efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Programmed death 1-blocking antibody, nivolumab, plus lymphocyte-activation gene 3-blocking antibody, relatlimab, is approved for advanced melanoma. We report results from Part 2 of RELATIVITY-104, the first phase II, proof-of-concept, head-to-head study to evaluate first-line nivolumab plus relatlimab plus platinum doublet chemotherapy (PDCT) versus nivolumab plus PDCT in patients with stage IV/recurrent non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In Part 2, patients were randomized 1:1 to nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT or nivolumab plus PDCT. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and duration of response (DOR) per BICR, ORR and PFS by subgroups, and safety. Exploratory analyses included overall survival (OS), biomarker, translational, and patient-reported outcomes. RESULTS: In part 2, the primary endpoint was not met (ORR, 51.3% for nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT versus 45.0% for nivolumab plus PDCT); PFS hazard ratio (HR; 90% confidence interval [CI]) was 0.89 (0.72 to 1.09). A trend towards improved clinical benefit was seen with nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT in a subgroup of patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) ≥1% and nonsquamous histology (ORR: 58.0% versus 39.6%; PFS: HR, 0.68; 90% CI 0.46 to 1.01). A potential improvement in OS was observed with nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT in the PD-L1 ≥1% nonsquamous subgroup (HR, 0.60; 90% CI 0.38 to 0.94). The safety profile of nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT was manageable and consistent with previous reports. CONCLUSION: In RELATIVITY-104, the addition of relatlimab to standard-of-care did not improve outcomes in the unselected all-randomized population. However, positive trends observed in the subgroup of patients with tumor PD-L1 ≥1% and nonsquamous NSCLC supports further investigation in these patients in the phase III RELATIVITY-1093 study. papers.abstract_en: Although aberrant glycosylation is closely associated with lung cancer (LC), salivary glycopatterns and their discriminatory value across healthy individuals, benign pulmonary disease, and LC remain insufficiently characterized. We profiled saliva from 307 participants using a lectin microarray, comprising a development cohort of 227 participants and an independent test cohort of 80 participants. Five task-specific LASSO-logistic regression models were constructed to distinguish pulmonary disease, LC, and LC subtypes. A separate Nom-LC model combined consensus lectin features selected by LASSO and support vector machine recursive feature elimination with clinical variables. Salivary glycopatterns differed among healthy volunteers, benign pulmonary disease, and LC groups, and the five task-specific models showed discriminatory performance across pulmonary disease, LC, and exploratory subtype classification tasks. The resulting Nom-LC model incorporated smoking history and four lectin signals (HHL, PNA, RCA120, and PWM), yielding AUCs of 0.908 and 0.907 in the training and internal validation sets. In the independent test cohort, the AUC was 0.903 (95% CI, 0.831-0.976); at the prespecified cutoff, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 86.36%, 94.44%, and 90.00%, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of salivary glycopatterns as an auxiliary tool for LC risk stratification, but prospective multicenter validation is required.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the stromal-immune circuits that coordinate matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the stromal-immune interactions associated with LUAD progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade. METHODS: Bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic data were integrated with clinical immunotherapy cohorts. Weighted gene co‑expression network analysis, survival meta‑analysis, and tissue enrichment scoring identified high‑risk cell subpopulations. Cell‑cell communication, virtual gene knockout, and spatial deconvolution were used to predict ligand‑receptor interactions and colocalization. Multiplex immunohistochemistry of clinical specimens validated spatial relationships. In vitro, MMP11-overexpressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and SPP1-overexpressing macrophages (Macs) were generated, and a macrophage-CAF co‑culture system was constructed. Migration, contractility, extracellular matrix deposition, and YAP/INHBA pathway activation was measured. In vivo, a murine tumor model was established and evaluated using in vivo imaging, flow cytometry, atomic force microscopy assay, HE, masson staining, and multiplexed IHC staining. RESULTS: MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic CAF (MMP11⁺ myCAF) was identified as a high-risk CAF subset enriched in primary tumor and metastatic lesions, characterized by elevated expression of matrix-remodeling and contractile genes, including MMP11, ACTA2, and TAGLN. Increased abundance of MMP11⁺ myCAF was associated with advanced tumor stage, metastasis, poor overall survival, and reduced benefit from immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Spatial transcriptomic deconvolution and multiplex immunohistochemistry revealed that MMP11⁺ myCAFs spatially co-localized with SPP1⁺ Mac, a pro-tumor myeloid population enriched in malignant and metastatic LUAD tissues. Ligand-receptor and downstream target analyses identified WNT5A as a key macrophage-derived mediator linking SPP1⁺ Mac to MMP11⁺ myCAF activation. Mechanistically, SPP1⁺ Mac exhibited activation of NFKB2/RELB-associated transcriptional programs, and SPP1 overexpression increased Nfkb2, Relb, and WNT5A protein levels in macrophages. WNT5A stimulation promoted YAP/INHBA-associated signaling in CAFs, enhancing CAF migration, contractility and extracellular matrix deposition. In animal models, activation of WNT5A signaling impaired the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1 blockade, reduced intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and increased MMP11⁺ CAF-associated collagen deposition and tissue stiffness. CONCLUSIONS: SPP1⁺ Mac-derived WNT5A may contribute to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy to overcome ICB resistance.

papers.abstract_en: The International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) established 26 consensus quality indicators (QIs) for lung cancer screening (LCS) programs, of which 20 were rated as essential and 6 as desirable by the expert panel. We evaluated the extent to which the American College of Radiology (ACR) Lung Cancer Screening Registry (LCSR), the largest LCS registry in the U.S., can support measurement of the IASLC QIs. We performed a crosswalk analysis, mapping all 26 IASLC QIs to the LCSR Data Dictionary and its 46 clinical performance measures, classifying each as directly measurable, derivable, or not measurable. The crosswalk was reviewed and independently validated by members of the ACR Early Lung Cancer Detection Registry Quality and Education Committee. Eight QIs (30.8%) were directly measurable, 10 (38.5%) were derivable, and 8 (30.8%) were not measurable from LCSR data alone. The LCSR therefore contains sufficient data elements to support measurement of approximately 69% of IASLC QIs. Remaining gaps involve screening uptake, clinical investigation, procedure complications, curative-intent treatment, treatment equity, diagnostic investigation equity and selected wait-time measures and would require additional registry fields or external data linkage.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Uniform radiation dose escalation has not improved outcomes in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and locoregional failure remains common despite multimodal therapy. We evaluated whether fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)-guided dose escalation to metabolically active tumor subvolumes reduces locoregional failure compared with standard chemoradiation. METHODS AND MATERIALS: PET-BOOST was a multi-institutional, open-label, phase 2 randomized trial conducted at 7 Canadian centers (January 2017-May 2022). Eligible patients had inoperable, FDG-avid stage IIIA/IIIB NSCLC and an achievable boost dose of at least 65 Gy. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard chemoradiation with 60 Gy in 30 fractions or metabolically adaptive radiotherapy with an integrated boost to FDG-avid subvolumes to a maximum of 85 Gy in 30 fractions. Concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy was planned, and consolidation durvalumab was permitted after 2018. The primary endpoint was 2-year locoregional failure; secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity, and quality of life (QOL). RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients were randomized: 40 to standard radiotherapy and 38 to dose escalation, with a median follow-up of 5.0 years. Median age was 64.4 years; 53% were male, 62% had stage IIIA disease, and 76% received consolidation durvalumab. Median prescription boost dose was 75 Gy. Two-year locoregional failure was 27.5% with standard radiotherapy versus 18.4% with dose escalation (P=.13). Two-year OS (72.5% vs. 73.7%; P=.91) and PFS (52.5% vs. 57.9%; P=.74) did not differ between arms. Grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicities occurred in 25% versus 37% of patients (P=.26), with one grade 5 pulmonary hemorrhage in the dose-escalation arm. QOL did not differ between arms. CONCLUSIONS: Metabolically adaptive PET-guided radiotherapy dose escalation was feasible in the context of consolidation immunotherapy and resulted in a numerically lower rate of locoregional failure, but did not significantly improve locoregional control or survival. The lower-than-anticipated event rate may have limited statistical power, and larger studies would be required to determine whether selective dose escalation provides a clinically meaningful improvement in locoregional control.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: We evaluated the preliminary efficacy of Empower LCS, a culturally-adapted multilevel intervention, compared with enhanced usual care (EUC) for improving LCS uptake among Hispanic patients. METHODS: In this pilot randomized controlled trial, Hispanic patients aged 50-80 years who met 2021 US Preventive Services Task Force LCS eligibility criteria were enrolled between February 2024 and August 2025. Participants were randomized 1:1 to EUC or Empower LCS. EUC included usual care plus a one-page educational handout. Empower LCS included a culturally adapted decision aid, provider notifications, patient text reminders, and health-related social needs support. The primary outcome was LDCT ordering within 4 months, assessed by medical record review or self-report. Analyses used chi-square tests and logistic regressions. RESULTS: Sixty patients were randomized (mean age, 60.8 years ± 7.4; 37/60 [61.7%] male; 21/60 [35.0%] Spanish-speaking). At 4 months, LDCT ordering was higher with Empower LCS than with EUC (15/30 [50.0%] vs 4/30 [13.3%]; p=0.002), as were LCS discussions (12/30 [40.0%] vs 5/30 [16.7%]; p=0.045). LDCT completion was higher but not significant (9/30 [30.0%] vs 4/30 [13.3%]; p=0.117), likely due to small sample size. In exploratory adjusted models, Empower LCS was associated with higher odds of LCS ordering (OR, 7.32; 95% CI, 1.97-34.16), and discussion (OR, 4.1; 95% CI, 1.20-16.28). Qualitative interviews identified provider trust and logistical barriers as drivers of screening engagement and completion, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Empower LCS increased LDCT ordering and screening discussions in this pilot trial. These findings support culturally tailored, low-cost, scalable interventions to reduce disparities in LCS participation.

papers.abstract_en: Cellular heterogeneity and plasticity are hallmarks of cancer that contribute to tumor growth and therapy resistance. Here, we investigated metabolic heterogeneity in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive cancer type with considerable plasticity between neuroendocrine (NE) and non-NE cellular states. Through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, we identified a universal dependency on exogenous cysteine/cystine (Cys) across all NE/non-NE SCLC cell states. Notably, NE and non-NE cells with low ASCL1 transcription factor levels underwent ferroptosis upon Cys depletion, whereas ASCL1high cells underwent apoptosis while remaining resistant to ferroptosis. This ferroptosis resistance was driven by the direct transcriptional activation of GCH1 by ASCL1, resulting in increased levels of the antioxidants BH4/BH2. Accordingly, combined Cys depletion and inhibition of BH4/BH2 synthesis reduced tumor growth in patient-derived xenografts. These findings demonstrate that metabolic state influences cell-death susceptibility in SCLC and provide a rationale for therapeutic strategies that exploit these metabolic differences.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acquired resistance significantly limits the long-term clinical benefit of osimertinib in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, the early non-genetic adaptations and microenvironmental crosstalk that enable initial tumor survival remain poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate the epigenetic-immune mechanisms driving osimertinib resistance and to identify novel actionable therapeutic targets. METHODS: We integrated transcriptomic profiling and clinical cohort analyses to identify therapy-induced secreted factors during the evolution of EGFR-TKI resistance. The upstream regulatory mechanisms were characterized using ChIP, Co-IP, and dual-luciferase reporter assays. The dual functional roles of the identified factor, serum amyloid A1 (SAA1), in tumor-intrinsic signaling and macrophage polarization were investigated in vitro. Finally, the therapeutic efficacy of combining SAA1 neutralization with osimertinib was evaluated across patient-derived organoids, xenografts, and immunocompetent spontaneous lung tumor models. RESULTS: We identified SAA1 as a critical therapy-induced secreted factor that progressively increases during the transition from drug tolerance to established resistance, which negatively correlates with clinical outcomes in patients receiving osimertinib. Mechanistically, osimertinib treatment suppressed the ERK-dependent phosphorylation of the transcriptional repressor GATAD2A at Ser114. This event destabilized the NuRD complex, thereby relieving the epigenetic transcriptional repression of SAA1. Secreted SAA1 promoted therapeutic resistance through dual mechanisms: activating the autocrine TLR4/NF-κB survival signaling in tumor cells and inducing the paracrine polarization of pro-tumorigenic SPP1⁺ macrophages. Therapeutically, targeted neutralization of SAA1 synergized robustly with osimertinib to reverse immunosuppressive remodeling and induce profound tumor regression in multiple preclinical models. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings define a novel therapy-induced ERK/GATAD2A/SAA1 epigenetic-immune axis that drives acquired resistance to osimertinib. SAA1 acts as a pivotal bridge between tumor-intrinsic survival adaptations and microenvironmental immune suppression, highlighting SAA1 neutralization as a tractable combinatorial strategy to enhance EGFR-TKI efficacy in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) is widely used as an early respiratory support strategy for adults with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF). Although HFNC may reduce the risk of endotracheal intubation, it remains uncertain whether the available evidence is sufficiently mature and whether this potential benefit translates into improved survival. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA) and GRADE assessment to assess HFNC versus standard oxygen therapy (SOT) in adult AHRF. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to March 31, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of HFNC versus SOT in adults with AHRF were included. The primary and secondary outcomes were endotracheal intubation and all-cause mortality, respectively. For each dichotomous outcome, the risk ratio (RR) with a 95% confidence interval (CI) was pooled using a random-effects model. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed. TSA was performed for intubation, and evidence certainty was assessed using GRADE. RESULTS: Ten independent RCTs reported across 11 publications were included. Compared with SOT, HFNC was associated with a lower risk of endotracheal intubation (RR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.77-0.93; P < 0.01; I² = 40%), but did not reduce all-cause mortality (RR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.88-1.16; P = 0.85; I² = 0%). Subgroup analyses suggested a lower intubation risk with HFNC among non-immunocompromised patients, patients with COVID-19, and those with baseline PaO₂/FiO₂ ≤ 200 mmHg, although no statistically significant subgroup interactions were observed. In the primary TSA, the accrued sample size represented only 36.8% of the diversity-adjusted required information size. The cumulative Z-curve crossed the conventional significance boundary, but not the trial sequential monitoring boundary. TSA sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings, indicating that current evidence remains inconclusive. GRADE certainty was low for endotracheal intubation and moderate for all-cause mortality. CONCLUSIONS: HFNC may reduce the risk of endotracheal intubation compared with SOT in adults with AHRF, but a survival benefit has not been demonstrated.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Comparative evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of almonertinib in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains fragmented across randomized and real-world studies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to comprehensively evaluate the comparative clinical performance of almonertinib. METHODS: Eight electronic databases were systematically searched from inception to March 2025. Comparative studies evaluating almonertinib versus active control regimens in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and treatment-related adverse events. Methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and analogous domains for observational studies, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. RESULTS: Fifteen comparative studies involving 1,902 patients met the eligibility criteria. Compared with control regimens, almonertinib was associated with higher pooled ORR (RR = 1.33, 95% CI 1.08-1.65) and DCR (RR = 1.14, 95% CI 1.03-1.26). However, after trim-and-fill adjustment for potential publication bias, the 95% CIs for both ORR and DCR included the null value, suggesting that the observed response benefits may be influenced by small-study effects. No statistically significant differences were observed for pooled PFS or OS. Almonertinib demonstrated a generally favorable safety profile, with a lower incidence of diarrhea, while rates of grade ≥3 adverse events and other major toxicities were broadly comparable between groups. Integrated analyses further suggested consistent concordance between ORR and DCR across most studies, supporting improved short-term disease control despite moderate-to-substantial between-study heterogeneity. CONCLUSION: Current comparative evidence suggests that almonertinib may improve tumor response and disease control while maintaining a favorable tolerability profile in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. Although favorable objective response outcomes were observed, these benefits may be influenced by small-study effects, and definitive survival advantages remain uncertain. These findings support almonertinib as a clinically meaningful therapeutic option, while underscoring the need for cautious interpretation and for larger, high-quality comparative trials with longer follow-up to further define its long-term clinical value. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Gastrin regulates gastric acid secretion and increases when gastric acidity is reduced. Erlotinib, a small-molecule inhibitor used to treat patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), has a pH-dependent absorption. We therefore investigated whether elevated gastrin levels, for example, due to proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use or achlorhydria, are associated with reduced erlotinib absorption. METHODS: Data of patients treated with erlotinib for NSCLC that were included in two previously conducted pharmacokinetic studies were used for this pharmacological proof-of-principle analysis. In these studies, patients were randomized to PPI use or not. Gastrin levels were quantified in samples drawn just before intake of erlotinib and used to study correlations with erlotinib concentrations. The pharmacokinetic endpoints area under the curve (AUC), trough concentration, and maximum concentration (Cmax) were correlated to gastrin concentrations and compared in patients with and without hypergastrinemia (gastrin ≥ 150 pg/mL). RESULTS: A total of 52 patients on erlotinib were included. Gastrin showed a significant inverse correlation with erlotinib AUC0-12h (r = -0.277; p = 0.047) and Cmax (r = -0.423; p = 0.002). In 11 patients with hypergastrinemia (gastrin ≥ 150 pg/mL), median erlotinib Cmax was > 30% lower (1890 ng/mL vs 1200 ng/mL; p = 0.024). The median AUC0-12h and AUC0-24h of erlotinib showed a non-significant trend towards lower AUCs of, respectively, 29% (p = 0.087) and 23% (p = 0.074), in patients with hypergastrinemia. papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: The biological basis distinguishing thymomas from thymic carcinomas (TCs) remains incompletely defined, despite longstanding efforts to interpret thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) in relation to thymic epithelial cell (TEC) differentiation. We integrated single-cell transcriptomic, immunohistochemical, and bulk transcriptomic analyses to define TEC programs associated with TET subtypes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We reanalyzed a publicly available human thymus single-cell RNA-seq dataset to define signature genes of TEC subclusters. Immunohistochemistry was performed on non-neoplastic thymus across developmental stages and on 83 TETs. Transcriptomic analyses were conducted using the TCGA-THYM cohort comprising 117 TETs. RESULTS: We identified an adult-enriched TEC subset with an aged progenitor-like program, marked by monoamine oxidase A (MAOA). Strikingly, MAOA immunohistochemistry highlighted spindle-shaped epithelial cells in the involuted adult thymus and in type A/AB thymomas. Most type B3 thymomas also exhibited broad MAOA reactivity, whereas TCs were negative or showed only scattered tumor-cell staining. Furthermore, MAOA immunostaining complemented KIT in the distinction between thymomas and TCs. In the TCGA-THYM cohort, MAOA expression reproduced these subtype-associated patterns and correlated with aged progenitor signatures. TEC signature scoring further revealed enrichment of aged progenitor-like programs in type A/AB thymomas, while type B3 thymomas concomitantly exhibited aged progenitor-like and cortical TEC-like signatures. In marked contrast, TCs showed low levels of aged progenitor scores but prominent mature medullary TEC signatures. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings refine the biological framework of TETs by linking thymomas to an aged progenitor-like TEC state. MAOA also offers practical diagnostic utility, particularly for distinguishing thymomas from TCs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer (SANO)-trial demonstrated that active surveillance is non-inferior to standard surgery in terms of two-year overall survival in patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). Active surveillance resulted in improved quality of life. Here, we report five-year outcomes. METHODS: From 2017 to 2021, a multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial was conducted. Patients with locally advanced oesophageal cancer who achieved complete clinical response (defined as no tumour detected on endoscopic biopsies, -ultrasound, or PET-CT) underwent active surveillance or standard surgery. Cox regression was used to compare five-year overall and disease-free survival, and the cumulative incidence of distant metastases was estimated using competing risk analysis. RESULTS: A total of 309 patients were included, 198 underwent active surveillance and 111 underwent standard surgery. Median follow-up was 76 months (IQR 67-86). Five-year overall survival was not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery (50%, 95%CI 43-57 vs. 54%, 95%CI 46-64; HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.77-1.77) with similar results across histologic subtypes. Disease-free survival was not statistically significantly different (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.94-2.06). The cumulative incidence of distant metastases at five years was significantly higher in the active surveillance group compared to the standard surgery group (46%, 95%CI 39-53 vs. 29%, 95%CI 21-37; P<.01). Overall, 85 of 198 patients (43%) avoided oesophagectomy, including those with sustained complete clinical response at last follow-up or distant metastases detected within six months after nCRT. CONCLUSIONS: Overall survival at five years is not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery in patients with oesophageal cancer and a complete clinical response after nCRT, despite a higher incidence of distant metastases in the active surveillance group. These findings support active surveillance as a feasible treatment strategy in selected patients.

papers.abstract_en: Paclitaxel (PTX) resistance is a major obstacle in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The metabolic enzyme phosphoglycerate mutase 1 (PGAM1) is implicated in chemoresistance, but its role in PTX resistance and cuproptosis remains unknown. We analyzed PGAM1 expression in PTX-resistant NSCLC cells and patient cohorts, performed truncation mapping and co-immunoprecipitation, and evaluated the PGAM1/PP2A/AKT/β-catenin/ATP7B axis. Drug sensitivity and cuproptosis were assessed in vitro, in patient-derived organoids (PDOs), and in xenograft models using the PGAM1 inhibitor HKB99. We identified that PGAM1 is overexpressed in PTX-resistant NSCLC and correlates with poor prognosis. PGAM1 overexpression reduces PTX sensitivity and confers cuproptosis resistance. Mechanistically, PGAM1 binds PP2A via its 1-150 region (critical residues V81, R83, N135, D144), inhibiting PP2A and enhancing AKT/GSK3β phosphorylation. This stabilizes β-catenin and promotes its nuclear translocation, where β-catenin/TCF4 drives ATP7B transcription. Elevated ATP7B lowers intracellular copper, impairs DLAT oligomerization, and confers resistance to elesclomol-induced cuproptosis. Pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PGAM1 restored PP2A activity, re-sensitized PTX-resistant NSCLC cells to paclitaxel, and re-engaged cuproptosis. These effects were rescued by reconstitution with wild-type PGAM1, but not with the PP2A-binding-deficient mutant, indicating that PTX resistance is driven by the scaffolding function of PGAM1. The therapeutic potential of this strategy was validated in PDOs and xenograft models, where HKB99 synergized with PTX to suppress the growth of resistant tumors. In conclusion, PGAM1 drives PTX resistance by enabling cuproptosis evasion through the PP2A/AKT/β-catenin/ATP7B axis; combining PGAM1 inhibition with PTX represents a promising strategy for refractory NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Cisplatin (DDP) resistance remains a major obstacle in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). This study investigates whether M2 macrophage‑derived exosomal miR‑3662 contributes to DDP resistance and uncovers the underlying mechanism. miR‑3662 was upregulated in LUAD tissues, further elevated in DDP‑resistant specimens and cell lines, and correlated with poor prognosis. Functionally, miR‑3662 overexpression enhanced DDP tolerance, clonogenicity, proliferation, and autophagy‑related activity while suppressing apoptosis; miR‑3662 inhibition reversed these effects. M2 macrophage exosomes transferred miR‑3662 into LUAD cells and promoted resistance, whereas GW4869 treatment or depletion of exosomal miR‑3662 attenuated this protection. Mechanistically, miR‑3662 directly bound the IRF8 3'UTR and reduced IRF8 protein expression. IRF8 occupied the RASSF5 promoter and activated its transcription. Consequently, miR‑3662‑mediated downregulation of the IRF8/RASSF5 axis induced cytoprotective autophagy. Restoration of IRF8 or RASSF5 counteracted M2‑exosome‑induced autophagy and resensitized cells to DDP. In xenograft models, targeting exosomal miR‑3662 restored IRF8/RASSF5 signaling, reduced autophagy markers, suppressed tumour growth, and improved DDP efficacy. These findings identify a novel microenvironment‑derived vesicular pathway where M2 macrophage exosomal miR‑3662 drives DDP resistance via IRF8/RASSF5 inhibition and autophagy activation, providing new insights into potential therapeutic strategies for overcoming platinum resistance in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of night shift-induced fatigue on radiology residents' diagnostic performance and to assess whether AI assistance offsets potential performance loss. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective intra-individual reader study, ten radiology residents (mean experience: 35 months; three women) interpreted three sets of 33 chest radiographs before and after a first-call on-site night shift. Sessions included two pre-shift readings (morning/afternoon, without AI) and two post-shift readings (morning, with/without AI). Eye tracking captured fixation duration and saccade count, and fatigue was defined as a ≥ 5% reduction in the slope of the saccadic main sequence between pre- and post-shift sessions. Diagnostic accuracy (Cohen's κ vs. expert majority vote), efficiency (mean reporting time per radiograph), eye-tracking metrics, and user surveys were analyzed with generalized linear mixed models and post-hoc Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons. RESULTS: Six of ten radiology residents were classified as fatigued, among whom diagnostic accuracy declined significantly post-shift (from κ = 0.71 ± 0.05 to κ = 0.61 ± 0.10; p < 0.001), with reduced fixation duration (p = 0.010) and saccade count (p = 0.015). Non-fatigued readers showed a smaller decline in accuracy (from κ = 0.72 ± 0.03 to κ = 0.65 ± 0.03; p = 0.037). Reporting times remained stable pre- and post-shift (p ≥ 0.463). AI assistance did not significantly improve diagnostic accuracy (Δκ = 0.03-0.04; p ≥ 0.525). Reporting times were numerically shorter with AI assistance in fatigued readers (Δ6.3 s; p = 0.122) and significantly shorter in non-fatigued readers (Δ9.9 s; p = 0.031). Surveys indicated mental exhaustion and reduced focus in fatigued readers. CONCLUSION: Night-shift-induced fatigue impaired diagnostic accuracy without slowing reporting speed, raising patient safety concerns. The utilized AI model did not restore pre-shift performance. KEY POINTS: Question Night-shift-induced fatigue may reduce diagnostic accuracy of radiology residents in chest radiography, yet its objective quantification and the compensatory potential of AI assistance remain unclear. Findings Fatigue, based on eye-tracking measurements of oculomotor efficiency, reduced diagnostic accuracy after night shifts without slowing reporting speed; AI assistance did not significantly improve accuracy. Clinical relevance Night-shift-induced fatigue can lower diagnostic accuracy in chest radiography despite unchanged reporting speed, posing patient-safety risks. The AI model used in this study cannot fully compensate for fatigue-related performance decline.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pre-existing psychiatric disorders have been associated with the severity of acute respiratory infections, including COVID-19, particularly in hospitalized populations. However, the underlying mechanisms, especially in community-based populations, remain unknown, limiting preparedness for future pandemics. We investigated the role of genetic liability for psychiatric disorders and related traits in COVID-19 and other respiratory infection severity among individuals reporting SARS-CoV-2 testing and available respiratory symptom data. METHODS: We included population-based cohort data from Denmark, Estonia, Iceland, Norway, and the United Kingdom (N = 78,507; 62% female; 41% SARS-CoV-2-positive; May 2020-March 2023). Respiratory infection severity was defined by self-reported days bedridden and an eleven-symptom composite score during the acute illness phase. Polygenic scores (PGSs) for eight psychiatric disorders and the personality trait neuroticism indexed genetic liability. Meta-analysed estimates from stepwise-adjusted regression analyses controlling for education, lifestyle, and psychiatric and somatic diagnosis history were used to assess associations between PGSs and acute respiratory infection severity, stratified by COVID-19 status. RESULTS: Higher genetic liability to insomnia, major depression (MD), and neuroticism was consistently associated with longer time bedridden (relative risk ratios per 1 SD change in PGS: 1.07-1.14, 95% confidence intervals [CIs]: 1.03-1.21) and more symptoms (incident rate ratios [IRRs]: 1.02-1.04, 95% CIs: 1.01-1.05) due to COVID-19. PGSs for insomnia, MD, neuroticism, anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia were also linked to higher non-COVID-19 symptom count (IRRs: 1.01-1.05, 95% CIs: 1.00-1.07). These associations remained robust after adjustment for lifestyle, education and medical comorbidities. Individuals in the highest MD PGS decile reported 20% more symptoms in non-COVID-19 illness and 10% more in COVID-19 compared with the bottom decile. No consistent associations were detected with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, alcohol dependence and post-traumatic stress disorder. No genetic link was observed with ischaemic heart disease or type 2 diabetes. CONCLUSIONS: Shared genetics may contribute to the link between psychiatric conditions and respiratory infection severity in community settings. Our results underscore the role of psychiatric genetic liability, beyond diagnosed psychiatric disorders, in contributing to both COVID-19 and other respiratory infection severity. These findings provide insights that may improve future risk stratification and public health strategies targeting respiratory viruses.

papers.abstract_en: Ionizing radiation (IR) induces oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation with ferroptosis contributing to radiation-induced cancer cell death. Peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6), a multifunctional enzyme involved in phospholipid repair and redox regulation, has been implicated in ferroptosis regulation, but its role in the radiosensitivity of cancer cells remains unclear. Here, we show that PRDX6 depletion enhances radiosensitivity in A549 lung cancer cells. PRDX6-silenced A549 cells exhibited elevated lipid peroxidation and labile iron levels, indicating a ferroptosis-prone state that was amplified by radiation. To identify the underlying drivers of ferroptosis sensitivity in the PRDX6 background, we performed global proteomic profiling of PRDX6-silenced A549 cells, with and without radiation. Basal PRDX6-deficient cells displayed increased levels of ACSL4 and DHCR7. ACSL4 activates peroxidation-prone polyunsaturated fatty acids for incorporation into membrane phospholipids, and DHCR7 depletes the antiferroptotic moiety, 7-dehydrocholesterol. MPST, an antioxidant protein, was downregulated. These changes were accentuated upon IR exposure with further suppression of GINS4, a negative regulator of ferroptosis. Functional rescue by oleic acid suggested the role of ACSL4 in the observed phenotypes. Radiosensitization via ferroptosis induction was additionally demonstrated in another human lung cancer cell line under the PRDX6-silenced state. Collectively, PRDX6 loss remodels the cellular proteome to establish a presensitized redox and lipid compositional state, which favors ferroptosis-driven radiosensitivity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Haematitum is a mineral-based traditional Chinese medicine widely used in clinical applications. Both the Chinese Materia Medica and modern research indicate that it exhibits lung toxicity and should not be administered over prolonged periods. The precise mechanism underlying this toxicity, however, remains incompletely understood. PURPOSE: This study aims to systematically elucidate the toxic mechanism of lung injury induced by Haematitum administration, emphasizing the central role of the gut-lung axis in this process. METHODS: The mouse model of lung injury induced by Haematitum was established. A combination of 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, and single-cell RNA sequencing was utilized to comprehensively analyze alterations in the intestinal microbiota, lung tissue metabolism, and lung cell atlas. The pharmacological validation was conducted by administering PPARγ agonists and TNF-α inhibitors. Furthermore, the detoxification effect of its classical combination with Inula japonica Thunb. was also evaluated. RESULTS: High-dose Haematitum disrupted the intestinal barrier and induced dysbiosis. Metabolites from the gut microbiota entered the bloodstream and exerted a pathogenic effect. Correlation analysis showed that gut microbiota dysbiosis is strongly associated with the pulmonary glycerophospholipid metabolic pathway. Results from single-cell sequencing and macrophage/TNF-α colocalization experiments indicated that the macrophages' PPAR signaling pathway was inhibited, inactivating their anti-inflammatory function and triggering the release of inflammatory factors such as TNF-α. Acting as a key messenger, TNF-α activated the TNF signaling pathway in neutrophils, driving them to acquire a highly destructive phenotype. The synergy between macrophages and neutrophils ultimately provoked inflammation and cell apoptosis in lung tissue. Pharmacological intervention of the PPARγ/TNF-α axis can effectively reverse cellular abnormalities and significantly alleviate lung injury. The combination with Inula japonica Thunb. also reduced lung toxicity, and components within this herb are predicted to act as natural PPARγ agonists. CONCLUSIONS: This study has revealed a potential toxic mechanism. The intestinal barrier in mice was compromised, with an increase in the relative abundance of Klebsiella, entry of microbial metabolites into the bloodstream, and disruption of glycerophospholipid metabolism in the lungs, which in turn resulted in dysfunction of pulmonary immune cells. It clarifies that the core mechanism of Haematitum-induced lung injury lies in inhibiting the PPAR signaling pathway in macrophages and activating the TNF signaling pathway in neutrophils. Administering Haematitum at a common dose or in combination with Inula japonica Thunb. mitigates these safety risks. These findings advance understanding of the toxicology of mineral-based medicines and provide a reference for the safe clinical application of these traditional Chinese medicines.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: FHL2 is an oncogenic scaffold protein that is overexpressed in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), making it a promising therapeutic target. SHK, a natural naphthoquinone, exhibits antitumor activity, but its molecular mechanism in LUAD, particularly its relationship with FHL2, remains unclear. AIM OF THIS STUDY: The present study aimed to define the effects of SHK on NSCLC and identify the potential underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: The anti-tumor effects of SHK were evaluated in LUAD cell lines (A549andH1299) and a patient-derived xenograft (PDX) model using CCK-8, colony formation, Transwell, and flow cytometry assays. Integrated proteomics, bioinformatics, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSAs) were employed to identify the direct target of SHK. The underlying mechanism was investigated through co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), Western blotting, qRT-PCR, cycloheximide (CHX) chase assays, and immunofluorescence/immunohistochemiscal (IF/IHC) staining. RESULTS: In both in vitro and PDX models, SHK potently inhibited LUAD growthand metastasisand induced cell death. At the molecular level, FHL2 was identified as a direct target of SHK. The direct binding of SHK to FHL2 promoted its proteasomal degradation, thereby disrupting the FHL2-FOXO1 complex. The dissociation of this complex increased FOXO1 acetylation and promoted its nuclear translocation, leading to the subsequent activation of the caspase cascade and apoptosis. CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate a novel signaling pathway through which SHK inhibits LUAD: by directly targeting FHL2 for degradation, SHK disrupts the FHL2-FOXO1 complex, which activates FOXO1-mediated transcription and triggers apoptosis. This study not only provides mechanistic insight into the antitumor function of SHK but also identifies the FHL2-FOXO1 axis as a potential therapeutic target for LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces lung cancer-specific and all-cause mortality, yet uptake remains low. This study evaluates LungCheck, a theory-informed multicomponent behavior change and implementation strategy designed to increase LDCT ordering in two diverse primary care settings. METHODS: This pilot study compared 16-month pilot and pre-pilot periods at a federally qualified health center (FQHC) and an academic faculty practice in New York City. LungCheck comprised educational meetings, materials and clinician reminders, an implementation blueprint, patient navigation, and EHR modifications. LDCT ordering rates (primary outcome) were compared using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Post-implementation surveys assessed acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. RESULTS: A total of 5,918 patient-period observations were included (1,569 academic; 4,349 FQHC). Among patients with documented LCS eligibility, the odds of LDCT ordering were significantly higher during the pilot at both the academic practice (OR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.47-4.85; p=0.001) and FQHC (OR, 4.53; 95% CI, 2.29-8.94; p<0.001). A combined-site multivariable model adjusting for site, age, sex, and race confirmed higher odds of LDCT ordering during the pilot (OR, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.44-2.63; p<0.001). Among patients with an LDCT order, completion was 71.4% (10/14) pre-pilot versus 35.7% (15/42) during the pilot at the academic practice and 42.9% (18/42; 95% CI, 28%-59%) versus 39.3% (24/61; 95% CI, 27%-53%) at the FQHC. The strategy was rated as highly acceptable (AIM, 4.47/5), appropriate (IAM, 4.44/5), and feasible (FIM, 4.41/5). DISCUSSION: LungCheck was associated with significantly increased LDCT ordering at both sites, high acceptability, feasibility, and appropriateness ratings and high provider knowledge, confidence, and perceived skills related to LCS. Although a corresponding improvement in LDCT completion was not observed, the small number of LDCT orders limited the precision of completion estimates. Persistent environmental and patient-level barriers underscore the need to adapt LungCheck into a multilevel intervention addressing patient-, provider, and system-level barriers across the LCS continuum, to be evaluated in a future cluster randomized trial.

papers.abstract_en: HNF4α-positive, TTF-1-negative lung adenocarcinomas represent a major subset of non-terminal respiratory unit (non-TRU) tumors with gastrointestinal-type differentiation and frequent KRAS mutations; however, their structural and microenvironmental diversities remain unclear. We herein examined 114 HNF4α-positive lung adenocarcinomas, including tumors with and without interstitial pneumonia (IP). IP-associated cases were analyzed separately. Tumors were classified into three low-power architectural patterns: Alveolar-preserving (A-type), Radial-traction (R-type), and Mass-forming destructive (M-type). In IP-absent cases, in which it was possible to reliably evaluate tumor contours and the mass effect, these architectural patterns closely corresponded to the three computed tomographic growth patterns defined by tumor-lung interactions-Replacement, Spiculated, and Expansive growth-indicating the potential of computed tomographic morphology to serve as a surrogate for the underlying architecture. A-type tumors showed strong gastric differentiation with high MUC6 expression and low frequencies of pleural, lymphatic, and vascular invasion, whereas R-type and M-type tumors exhibited progressively lower MUC6 expression, more prominent intestinal differentiation, and higher rates of lymph node metastasis, particularly in M-type, representing more aggressive phenotypes. KRAS mutations were detected across all three patterns but were less frequent in M-type; KRAS G12C was enriched in A-type tumors. M-type tumors showed the poorest disease-free and overall survival irrespective of spread through air spaces (STAS) status. Despite their indolent-appearing architecture, among STAS-positive tumors, A-type was associated with worse disease-free and overall survival than R-type, identifying STAS-positive A-type as a high-risk subset within the HNF4α-positive non-TRU spectrum. RNA sequencing further identified three distinct gene expression clusters corresponding to epithelial-mesenchymal transition-related, angiogenic/tumor-associated macrophage-rich, and mucinous epithelial programs. STAS-positive A-type tumors predominantly belonged to the angiogenic/tumor-associated macrophage-rich group, implicating this microenvironment in their aggressive behavior. Since STAS-positive A-type tumors may present as radiologically indolent replacement-growth lesions, careful evaluation of resected specimens and close postoperative surveillance are warranted.

papers.abstract_en: Radon exposure is the leading cause of lung cancer among nonsmokers, posing a significant public health risk. Despite its known dangers, population-wide exposure assessments of indoor radon have been limited by the reliance on area-based summaries, such as average and median concentrations, which ignore the distributional characteristics of small areas. This study developed a national-scale modeling framework to estimate ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA)-level distributions of indoor radon concentrations across the contiguous United States from 2000 to 2021. We utilized over six million short-term radon measurements, which were aggregated at the ZCTA level to predict percentiles. By further modeling within-ZCTA radon exposure distributions, we improved the quantification of exposure heterogeneity and were able to estimate the proportion and number of residents exceeding policy-relevant exposure thresholds more accurately. The results reveal that approximately half of U.S. ZCTAs have at least one in five households exposed to radon concentrations exceeding the Environmental Protection Agency's action level (148 Bq/m3), with high-exposure areas predominantly located in the Midwest. These findings provide crucial data to help residents recognize their potential radon risk, urge policymakers to design cost-effective interventions, and offer health researchers an essential database for incorporating within-ZCTA radon exposure distributions into health risk assessments.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Pemetrexed, a standard antifolate chemotherapy for non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), is often limited by acquired resistance. We investigated whether SRC kinase mediates pemetrexed resistance and whether SRC inhibition can suppress survival signaling in pemetrexed-resistant NSCLC cells. METHODS: Pemetrexed-resistant cell lines (PC9 R, NCI-H460 R, and NCI-H3122 R) were generated through chronic pemetrexed exposure. Protein phosphorylation profiling and Western blotting identified key signaling alterations. SRC was abrogated using transient and doxycycline-inducible CRISPR/Cas9 systems, and reciprocal siRNA knockdown of SRC and thymidylate synthase (TS) was performed. Three SRC inhibitors-dasatinib, bosutinib, and saracatinib-were assessed using cell viability, colony formation, apoptosis, and cell cycle assays. RESULTS: All pemetrexed-resistant cell lines demonstrated elevated phosphorylated SRC (p-SRC Y416) and enhanced downstream signaling. SRC knockout reduced p-SRC Y416, p-STAT3, and p-FAK, while increasing markers of DNA damage (γ-H2AX) and apoptosis (cleaved caspase-3), impairing cell viability and clonogenicity. SRC knockdown reduced TS expression in two resistant models, whereas TS knockdown did not suppress p-SRC Y416. Among SRC inhibitors, dasatinib showed the most potent, dose-dependent suppression of SRC signaling. Dasatinib also induced G0/G1 arrest, DNA damage, and apoptosis, thereby reducing colony formation. CONCLUSION: SRC activation is a critical mechanism of acquired pemetrexed resistance in NSCLC and may contribute to resistance through TS-associated survival signaling. SRC inhibition, particularly with dasatinib, disrupts pro-survival pathways and promotes DNA damage-mediated cell death in pemetrexed-resistant cells. These findings support further investigation of SRC inhibitors, alone or with pemetrexed, as a biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy for SRC-activated pemetrexed-resistant NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Emerging evidence indicates that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are critical regulators of tumor radiosensitivity and hold promise as novel targets for radiosensitization. However, the underlying mechanisms by which most lncRNAs modulate radiosensitivity remain elusive. This study aimed to elucidate the functional significance and mechanistic basis of lncRNA MIR4435-2HG in regulating non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) radiosensitivity. Our findings demonstrated that ionizing radiation induced upregulation of lncRNA MIR4435-2HG. High expression of MIR4435-2HG was significantly associated with poor prognosis in patients with lung adenocarcinoma. Inhibition of MIR4435-2HG increased the radiosensitivity of NSCLC cells. Mechanistically, MIR4435-2HG acted as a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) to sponge miR-1-3p, thereby derepressing DNA-PKcs at both mRNA and protein levels. Knockdown of MIR4435-2HG impaired non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) repair, as evidenced by increased 53BP1 and γH2AX foci, reduced interaction of DNA-PKcs with Ku70 and XRCC4, and decreased NHEJ repair efficiency. Conversely, overexpression of MIR4435-2HG induced a radioresistant phenotype. Dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed the interaction between miR-1-3p and both MIR4435-2HG and DNA-PKcs. Rescue experiments confirmed that miR-1-3p overexpression reversed MIR4435-2HG-mediated DNA-PKcs upregulation, proliferation enhancement, and radioresistance. Notably, MIR4435-2HG selectively promoted error-prone NHEJ without affecting homologous recombination. In summary, our study delineates a novel and functionally specific ceRNA axis wherein MIR4435-2HG sequesters miR-1-3p to upregulate DNA-PKcs and selectively activate NHEJ-mediated DSB repair. These findings not only introduce a critical regulatory node into the DNA repair network but also position the MIR4435-2HG/miR-1-3p/DNA-PKcs axis as a promising predictive biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming radioresistance in NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Exon 19 mutations in the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase domain, including the common ΔE746-A750 deletion and the less frequent L747P substitution, are clinically important drivers of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although these mutations occur within the β3-αC region, how they alter EGFR conformational dynamics and influence the response to the covalent inhibitor afatinib remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated mutation-dependent changes in EGFR conformational ensembles, dual-mode of afatinib binding, and Cys797-mediated covalent reaction energetics in wild-type, ΔE746-A750, and L747P kinase domains. We find that both mutations preferentially stabilize active-like kinase conformations but do so through distinct structural mechanisms. The ΔE746-A750 deletion produces greater P-loop and ATP-pocket conformational heterogeneity, whereas L747P restricts αC-helix and activation-loop dynamics and more strongly stabilizes the active-like ensemble. Afatinib binding disrupts the K745-E762 interaction and alters the αC-helix conformation while the pre-formed covalent state samples αC-out configurations that increase accessibility of an αC-adjacent pocket that is less accessible in the apo state. Alchemical calculations further reveal mutation- and protonation-state-dependent differences in the conditional noncovalent binding free energy of afatinib. QM/MM calculations of Cys797-afatinib bond formation reveal mutation-dependent differences in the calculated reaction barrier, with L747P showing a lower barrier than ΔE746-A750 within the employed QM/MM model. Together, these results show that EGFR exon 19 mutations reshape the conformational landscape and local structural environment of the kinase, thereby influencing afatinib binding and the energetic environment of covalent bond formation. These findings provide a structural framework for understanding how distinct EGFR mutations can produce different responses to covalent kinase inhibition.

papers.abstract_en: In recent years, spectroscopic technology has become a key tool in clinical diagnosis. However, the traditional single-modal spectral analysis method often struggles to capture the full biochemical complexity of heterogeneous biological samples, resulting in limited chemical interpretability and diagnostic sensitivity. To address these challenges, a novel multimodal spectroscopic analysis framework called DeepSpectrum is proposed. It combines the Spectral Mamba and bidirectional gated recurrent unit architectures to enable high-precision lung cancer diagnosis. Specifically, the spectral signals are converted into multichannel image modalities using the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Gramian angular difference fields (GADF), thereby constructing rich multimodal data sets. Subsequently, the DeepSpectrum framework is trained, validated, and tested on multimodal spectral data sets, including Raman, Fourier transform infrared, UV-vis absorbance, and fluorescence spectra. It achieved accuracy rates of 98.1%, 98.5%, 92.0%, and 89.2% in lung cancer diagnosis, demonstrating broad applicability across spectral types and complex biological samples. Compared with 11 existing single-modal and multimodal methods, DeepSpectrum showed clear advantages across all evaluation metrics. To further explain the model's decision-making basis, weighted class activation mapping is used to analyze the spectral signals of normal and cancer samples. The model focuses on key regions such as 1127-1375 cm-1 (heme/hemoglobin vibrations) and 1447 cm-1 (lipid metabolism) in Raman spectra, as well as 1000-1140 cm-1 (nucleic acids) in FTIR spectra. These peak values correspond to the evolution process of lung cancer. This not only validates the biochemical interpretability of the DeepSpectrum model but also provides a reliable diagnostic tool for the precise clinical identification of lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: For clinical stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), treatment selection between surgery and stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) can be preference sensitive. Accordingly, we developed a web-based patient decision aid (PDA) and prospectively evaluated its patient-reported utility in routine respiratory clinical practice. METHODS: This prospective pilot study enrolled 26 patients with clinical stage I NSCLC or suspected primary lung cancer (cT1-2aN0M0) considered candidates for surgery and SBRT at two Japanese hospitals between October 2023 and December 2024. Patients used the PDA before finalizing treatment through shared decision-making. Outcomes were patient-perceived utility, Decisional Conflict Scale (DCS) scores measured once after the decision, and treatment preference transitions. RESULTS: Twenty-four patients completed the PDA evaluation. All participants reported improved knowledge or understanding, 18 (75.0%) reported reduced anxiety, and 23 (95.8%) reported that the PDA was useful. Final treatment selection was SBRT in 15 (57.7%), surgery in nine (34.6%), and observation in two (7.7%), with no significant difference by histological confirmation at enrollment (p = 0.59). In the exploratory post-decision DCS analysis of 22 patients, those who underwent surgery had numerically higher uncertainty scores than those who underwent SBRT (29.2 vs. 14.9). The PDA mainly clarified preferences among initially undecided patients. CONCLUSIONS: The web-based PDA was acceptable, and participants reported improved understanding and reduced anxiety. papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer shows wide variability in outcomes after curative-intent resection. 18F-FDG PET/CT is indispensable for staging but primarily reflects glucose metabolism rather than the invasion-related tumor biology that may contribute to recurrence. 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 PET/CT images the urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR), a cell-surface mediator of local invasion and metastatic spread. Methods: We conducted a single-center cohort study of patients with resectable lung adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma who were prospectively enrolled to undergo preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT in addition to standard-of-care 18F-FDG PET/CT. Primary tumor SUVmean and SUVmax were measured for both tracers, and tumor tissue uPAR expression was quantified by immunohistochemistry (H-score). Postoperative recurrence was the primary endpoint and was analyzed in a competing-risks framework with death as a competing event. The primary prognostic analyses evaluated 68Ga-uPAR SUVs, 18F-FDG SUVs, and uPAR H-score as continuous variables using univariable cause-specific Cox models. A 1.5-y horizon was used for exploratory Youden-derived high versus low groups, for which cumulative incidence of recurrence was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Trial registration number is NCT02755675 Results: Thirty-seven patients comprised the analysis cohort, of whom 14 developed recurrence during a median follow-up of 2.38 y (interquartile range, 1.97-8.20 y). Four patients died without prior recurrence. 68Ga-uPAR uptake correlated with tumor tissue uPAR expression, whereas 18F-FDG uptake did not. As continuous prognostic factors, higher 68Ga-uPAR SUVmax (hazard ratio, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.34-3.49; P = 0.002) and higher uPAR H-score (hazard ratio, 1.04 per unit; 95% CI, 1.01-1.08; P = 0.017) were associated with recurrence; 68Ga-uPAR SUVmean showed borderline evidence of association (P = 0.053), whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic. Exploratory 1.5-y threshold analyses showed greater early recurrence in the high SUVmean and high H-score groups; the SUVmax comparison did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion: Preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET uptake reflected tumor uPAR expression and was associated with early postoperative recurrence, whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic in this cohort. These findings suggest that uPAR PET captures invasion-related tumor biology that is not fully reflected by glucose metabolism imaging. External validation is required.

In vivo experiments demonstrated that upregulation of circ_FAM210A expression reduced both the size and weight of tumours in mice. CONCLUSION: Upregulation of circ_FAM210A expression can inhibit the malignant progression of NSCLC, partly through the miR-670-5p/SYNE3/apoptotic pathway axis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Adenocarcinoma (AC) is the leading histopathological type of lung cancer (LC), curative surgery being the cornerstone for the best survival results. However, even in the patients who had curative surgery, the survival outcomes differ. Spread through air spaces (STAS), recognized as a histopathological feature in the 2015 World Health Organization (WHO) Classification, causes poor survival outcomes in lung AC. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic impact of STAS on recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) in surgically resected T1-2N0 lung AC, with particular attention to its interaction with tumor size. METHODS: This single center retrospective study evaluates the effect of STAS on RFS and OS in 296 surgically resected T1-2N0 lung AC patients. For further analysis, patients were divided into four subgroups combining their STAS status and tumor size. RESULTS: STAS presence rate was 37.5%, which was associated with aggressive tumor characteristics, such as non-lepidic predominant subtypes, higher pathological T stage (pT), visceral pleura invasion (VPI), and lymphovascular invasion (LVI). OS and RFS were significantly worse in the STAS-Present (STAS-P) group (p = 0.030). Subgroup analysis revealed that STAS-P tumors > 2 cm had the worst outcomes, as expected. Notably, on univariate analysis STAS presence appeared most prognostically decisive in tumors ≤ 2 cm, in which there was no significant difference in survival between STAS-P tumors ≤ 2 cm and STAS-Absent (STAS-A) tumors > 2 cm. CONCLUSIONS: STAS was a significant prognostic factor on univariate analysis but did not retain independent significance after multivariable adjustment. In an exploratory subgroup analysis, STAS-P tumors ≤ 2 cm carried survival outcomes comparable to STAS-A tumors > 2 cm, suggesting STAS may attenuate the prognostic advantage of smaller tumor size. This hypothesis-generating finding warrants prospective validation before informing surgical management.

However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective design and potential residual confounding.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate changes in clinical, functional, and inflammatory parameters in patients with severe eosinophilic asthma receiving benralizumab treatment, to determine clinical remission rates, and to explore factors associated with clinical remission. Demographic characteristics, clinical findings, pulmonary function test results, peripheral blood eosinophil counts, and treatment responses were obtained from medical records. Baseline findings were compared with those obtained after at least 12 months of treatment. Clinical remission was defined as the absence of exacerbations, no maintenance oral corticosteroid use, well-controlled asthma, and stable or improved lung function. Factors associated with clinical remission were evaluated using multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression. RESULTS: The mean age of the 33 included patients was 54.6 ± 13.8 years, and 60.6% were female. After 12 months of treatment, clinical remission was achieved in 75.8% (25/33) of patients. Mean FEV₁ increased from 1514 mL to 2188 mL (+ 674 mL; p < 0.001), and FEV₁ (% predicted) improved from 54.9% to 76.8% (p < 0.001). papers.abstract_en: Smoking is associated with structural and functional alterations in the lungs, some of which may be reflected in quantitative imaging features. Radiomics enables the extraction of high-dimensional image-derived descriptors and may provide information beyond routinely available clinical variables. We investigated whether bilateral lung radiomics, both independently and integrated with clinical variables, could classify patient-level smoking status. An exploratory secondary analysis was also performed to assess whether radiomic and clinical feature representations could discriminate smoking exposure intensity among smokers. A total of 506 patients were included, comprising 253 smokers and 253 nonsmokers. Right and left lung radiomic features were extracted separately from visually normal-appearing lung parenchyma on thoracic CT images. Multiple feature representations were evaluated, including right lung radiomics, left lung radiomics, concatenated right-left radiomics, summary/asymmetry radiomics, clinical variables alone, and radiomics combined with clinical variables. Clinical variables included age, sex, height, weight, and body mass index. Pack-years were excluded from the binary smoking status classification models to avoid target-related information leakage. For each binary classification task, a balanced internal hold-out set containing 25 smokers and 25 nonsmokers was reserved, while the remaining patients were evaluated using stratified tenfold cross-validation. Four feature selection or dimensionality reduction strategies and five classifier families were assessed, resulting in 435 model configurations across the main cohort and sex-specific subgroup analyses. Threshold selection was performed using the Youden index derived from cross-validated out-of-fold predictions. For the exploratory smoking exposure analysis, 253 smokers with available pack-year information were categorized into < 10, 10-20, and > 20 pack-year groups and evaluated using pooled stratified tenfold cross-validation. The best-performing radiomics-based configurations showed higher discrimination than the clinical-only configuration. The clinical-only random forest model achieved a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.673 and a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.610. Among radiomics-only configurations, concatenated bilateral radiomics achieved a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.734 and a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.712. The strongest hold-out discrimination was obtained using concatenated bilateral radiomics combined with clinical variables, ReliefF feature selection, and stacking classification, achieving a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.803, balanced accuracy of 0.700, sensitivity of 0.720, and specificity of 0.680. Feature selection stability analysis showed that the final concatenated bilateral radiomics + clinical configuration retained five clinical variables and 15 radiomic features, several of which were repeatedly selected across cross-validation folds. Sex-specific subgroup analyses showed moderate but variable performance. In the exploratory three-class smoking exposure analysis, integrating left lung radiomics with clinical variables yielded the most balanced class-wise performance, achieving the highest balanced accuracy (0.658) and the highest sensitivity for the intermediate 10-20 pack-year group (0.417), although the clinical-only model achieved the highest macro-AUC. Bilateral lung radiomics showed potential for patient-level smoking status classification, particularly when combined with clinical variables. These findings suggest that quantitative imaging features could provide complementary information beyond routinely available patient-level variables. The exploratory smoking exposure analysis further suggested that radiomics + clinical configurations may contain limited information related to smoking exposure intensity, although intermediate exposure remained challenging to discriminate. However, the moderate performance, subgroup variability, and lack of external validation indicate that this approach should be considered investigational until confirmed in larger independent cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: Uniportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (uRATS) seeks to combine the dexterity of robotic platforms with reduced access trauma, yet its comparative value over multiportal RATS (mRATS) remains uncertain. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested differences in length of stay and operative time by comparator port count, potentially reflecting confounding by operative era and experience. A possible reduction in console time and early postoperative pain was observed, but these findings were based on very-low-certainty evidence and were sensitive to individual studies.

papers.abstract_en: Occult lymph node metastasis (OLM) remains a major clinical challenge in patients with lung cancer despite comprehensive preoperative staging efforts. Although several predictors of OLM, including tumor diameter, metabolic activity, molecular characteristics, and radiomics, have been extensively investigated, the predictive role of tumor volume remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate whether tumor volume, quantified semi-automatically using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted Synapse 3D software, could predict OLM in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer. Patients who underwent surgical resection for clinically staged cT1b-cN0M0 lung cancer between 2018 and 2024 were included. Tumor volume was quantified using Synapse 3D software. Associations between tumor volume and OLM were assessed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Because tumor diameter and tumor volume may introduce multicollinearity in multivariable models, separate receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. A total of 248 patients were included, of whom 59 (23.8%) were female. The mean age was 65.4 years. OLM were identified in 10.8%, 4.8%, and 2.0% of patients at the N1, N2a, and N2b nodal stations, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified younger age (p = 0.004), greater tumor volume (p = 0.01), and histopathological subtypes other than adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma as independent predictors of OLM. Tumor diameter, extent of resection, surgical approach, and PET-CT metabolic activity were not significantly associated with OLM. ROC analysis demonstrated that tumor volume had significantly greater discriminatory ability for predicting OLM than tumor diameter (AUC: 69% vs. 58%; DeLong test, p = 0.004). AI-assisted tumor volumetry is an independent predictor of occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Postoperative empyema with persistent air leak remains a challenging complication after pulmonary resection. Fenestration may be required in refractory cases but is highly invasive, particularly in high-risk patients. We report two patients successfully treated with prolonged open drainage using a large-sized cut tube without fenestration and propose clinical criteria for selecting suitable candidates. CASE PRESENTATION: A 72-year-old man with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis developed Aspergillus empyema with persistent air leak after bullectomy for pneumothorax, and a 71-year-old man developed empyema with persistent air leak after left lower lobectomy and lingulectomy with bronchoplasty for lung cancer. Both were initially treated with closed chest drainage and antimicrobial therapy. On days 23 and 32, respectively, after infection was controlled, drainage volume decreased to < 50 mL/day, the empyema cavity became localized, and residual lung expansion remained stable despite persistent air leakage, the drainage tubes were cut and shortened to convert them to open drainage. CT confirmed that both cavities were anatomically separated from the pulmonary artery and other major hilar vessels. Both patients were subsequently managed as outpatients, and the empyema cavities gradually became obliterated by granulation tissue, allowing tube removal without fenestration. No recurrence occurred during 2 and 4 years of follow-up, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged open drainage with a large-sized cut tube may provide a less invasive alternative to fenestration in selected patients with postoperative empyema and persistent air leak. Suitable candidates may be characterized by controlled infection, low drainage volume, a localized empyema cavity, stable residual lung expansion, and anatomical separation from major hilar vessels.

papers.abstract_en: BAP1 and HMGB1 alterations are implicated in the pathogenesis of mesothelioma, an aggressive cancer of the membranes covering the thoracic and abdominal cavities. Genetic inactivating mutations of BAP1 cause cancer in ~100% of carriers. The mechanism/s that regulate BAP1 expression were unknown. We discovered that HMGB1 directly modulates BAP1 expression. These findings were confirmed in lung, colon, and cholangiocarcinoma cell lines. These findings indicate that while BAP1 inactivating mutations promote cancer development, cancer cells that do not express BAP1 are less aggressive, pointing to the HMGB1-BAP1 axis as a novel attractive target for therapy. Furthermore, our discovery that HMGB1-driven BAP1 overexpression supports cancer growth provides a mechanistic rationale for the improved survival observed in mesothelioma patients with somatic BAP1 inactivating mutations.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, yet early diagnosis remains difficult, highlighting the need for sensitive, noninvasive methods. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their surface proteins (e.g., PD-L1) are promising biomarkers; nevertheless, current EV detection requires time-consuming purification, sophisticated instrumentation, and long measurement protocols, resulting in high expenses and operational difficulties. This study developed an integrated colorimetric sensor, IMAN, based on a strategy of "Immunomagnetic Microbeads (IM) capture + Aptamer(Apt) recognition + Nanozyme (N) catalysis". IMAN employs magnetic beads modified with antibodies against CD9 and CD81 to directly capture EVs from serum, eliminating the need for time-consuming prior isolation; combined with a one-step colorimetric readout, the entire workflow can be completed with only ∼40 min of hands-on time, requiring no complex instrumentation. The PD-L1 protein on the EV surface is specifically recognized by a nanoparticle-bound nucleic acid aptamer. Signal generation is achieved through the catalytic oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) by a platinum-gold bimetallic nanozyme (Pt@Au). The facile IMAN colorimetric method demonstrated a relatively broad dynamic range (107-1010 particles/mL), high specificity (unaffected by 100 pg/mL soluble PD-L1 in serum), and reproducibility (relative standard deviation, RSD = 9.1%). Analysis of clinical serum samples revealed significantly elevated EV-PD-L1 levels in patients with lung cancer compared with healthy donors and patients with benign nodule (p < 0.01). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis yielded areas under the curve (AUC) of 0.849 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from healthy donors and 0.860 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from patients with benign nodules, which are superior to those of the conventional serum biomarkers CEA and Cyfra21-1. By addressing the cost, complexity, and slow response of current methods, IMAN offers a simple, cost-effective platform for direct EV surface protein detection without complex instrumentation, providing a novel tool for the noninvasive lung cancer diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: Erlotinib hydrochloride (ERL), an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in non-small cell lung cancer, is a classic example of drug polymorphism. However, the influence of crystallisation methods, PLGA, and thermal ageing on its polymorphic behaviour remains unexplored. This study investigated ERL polymorphism in binary mixtures prepared by blending, co-grinding, and solvent evaporation. PXRD revealed that blending and co-grinding retained ERL polymorphic form A, whereas solvent evaporation yielded form B in all binary mixtures. Thermal ageing has a significant effect on ERL crystallinity. DSC melting endotherms for form A are at 213.75 and 233.26°C, whereas form B shows a single melting endotherm at 231.96°C. MDSC efficiently captured the melt-mediated recrystallisation of form A. Further, ATR-FTIR with chemometric analysis differentiated the polymorphs into form A (anti) and form B (syn) conformations based on spectral regions at 3270 cm⁻1 (non-classical H-bonding) and 2540 cm⁻1 (N⁺-H···Cl⁻ interactions). SEM revealed plate-like and needle-like morphologies for forms A and B, respectively. Conversely, saturation solubility results reported higher solubility for the solvent-evaporated drug, due to its crystal morphology. Drug content by RP-HPLC (98-102% w/w) confirmed that the observed changes were solely physical transitions. Overall, this study provides insights into the development of ERL-loaded PLGA microspheres.

In this study, we characterised 1-octen-3-ol, an active compound derived from bamboo leaves, as a bioactive natural compound with anti-LUSC activity. In vitro, 1-octen-3-ol significantly suppressed LUSC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis. Network pharmacology predicted the PI3K/AKT pathway as a central mediator of its activity. Mechanistic studies confirmed that 1-octen-3-ol inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, accompanied by increased expression of p53 and cleaved-caspase3. The PI3K agonist 740Y-P and AKT agonist SC79 partially reversed the effects of 1-octen-3-ol on LUSC cell migration, invasion, colony formation, and protein expression, underscoring the critical role of the PI3K/AKT pathway. In vivo, 1-octen-3-ol markedly suppressed LUSC xenograft growth, and its tumor-suppressive effect was abrogated by co-administration of either the PI3K or AKT agonist. This study is the first to demonstrate that 1-octen-3-ol exerts potent inhibition of LUSC progression via modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, thereby activating p53 and initiating caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the anti-LUSC activity of 1-octen-3-ol, a natural volatile small-molecule, and support further lead-discovery efforts based on natural-product sources.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains one of the most widespread and deadly malignancies worldwide, underscoring the urgent need for rapid and noninvasive diagnostic strategies.
